newsitem.title: UK: British exporting firms rally as pound falls.
newsitem.headline: British exporting firms rally as pound falls.

text.p: Surging shares in major exporting companies powered the British stock market to record highs on Thursday as the pound's stunning five-month rally apparently ended.

As the pound tumbled from four-year highs against the mark and dollar, there were hopes that the currency may at last have run out of steam, relieving the upward pressure on prices of British products on global markets.

The rising pound has cut the sterling value of profits that British companies earn abroad, prompting analysts to cut their profit expectations for companies as diverse as British Steel, Zeneca Group and ICI.
On Thursday, however, those three were among the biggest gainers as the blue chip FTSE 100 index leapt some 1.25 percent to an all-time peak of 4,273.4 points.
"The currency is having a major impact," said the head of equity trading at one London brokerage.
"There has been a swing round in sector interest, some of the stocks that have underperformed because of the currency have perked up while the domestics have weakened."

Sterling's inexorable rise since August ended in several earnings downgrades by brokers earlier this month as worries intensified that the currency's appreciation would hit profits of companies with big overseas earnings.
Many analysts halved their profit forecasts for British Steel and downgrades hit pharmaceutical, chemicals and home products shares.
But analysts said they were in no rush to revise estimates upwards given the historic volatility of sterling and fears that this retreat may be only a temporary respite.
"I'd need to see a sustained move to around 2.40 marks for a sustained period, maybe a few months, before I'd consider revisions," said one analyst.
The reversal in the pound, up some 20 percent against the German mark since August, came after a run of surprisingly weak economic figures.
Weak retail sales data on Wednesday heightened perceptions that British interest rates may not need to be raised ahead of national elections, which must be held by May 22.
The British currency steadied in European trading around 2.6675 against the German mark and at 1.6370 against the dollar.
Shares in British Steel, among the biggest hit by sterling's strength in recent weeks, jumped 2.5 percent.

Shares in chemicals giant ICI Plc climbed 1.8 percent. Shares in SmithKline Beecham and Glaxo Wellcome soared 4.3 percent and 3.6 percent, respectively, while shares in Zeneca Group and Grand Met each added three percent.
Another analyst, who recently cut his earnings estimates on some chemicals concerns, said he would probably review his forecasts in about six weeks.
